executiveSummary: Beesel's generated 2025 administrative inputs are coherent: 13,524 residents, eight neighbourhoods in two districts, two BAG woonplaatsen, three BRT settlements, Reuver station, ten grouped scheduled-transit stops and two A73-derived municipal links. The complete ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service deterministic contract passes, including exact no-event behavior, event-attributable deprived person-hours, service-layer-invariant local hazard and exact population/demand/delivery reconciliation. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The locally material Maas preset reports persistent exact impact from a three-line centroid screen without a selected breach, water depth, arrival time, current defence geometry or the Beesel dike reinforcement completed in 2022. Eight physically different nonzero hazards reuse exactly the same neighbourhood order. The mobility/supply graph omits the daily Reuver-Kessel motor ferry even though Beesel's observed 2021 high-water log documents its closure and reopening, leaving only north-south A73 links. Integration-ready public roads, traffic status, water works, provider areas, weather, river observations and flood-risk layers exist, but must retain official-context, official-scenario or observed provenance. Utility topology, operating state, crews, stocks, backup and restoration remain unavailable or security-sensitive and must stay unknown or transparently synthetic.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 and administrative geometries for GM0889
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0889 Beesel with 13,524 registered residents, density 485 residents per square kilometre, 26.0% aged 65 or older and 1,959 one-person households.

The app consumes annual CBS OData and PDOK 2025 municipality, district, neighbourhood and safety-region data under CC BY 4.0, plus BAG woonplaatsen under Public Domain Mark 1.0. These are official-context data, not live population, hazard or infrastructure observations.
Eight published neighbourhood populations sum to 13,515, nine below the municipality row (-0.067%); rounded official components require explicit reconciliation rather than silent replacement.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Machine-readable road, rail, scheduled-transit and current road-status context
supports: NWB is national official-context road geometry refreshed monthly under CC0. The generated network gives Beesel only two A73 links, to Venlo and Roermond, each with nominal scenario capacity 260; this is neither measured throughput nor emergency passability.

ProRail CC0 geometry identifies Reuver station. OVapi feed 9543, retrieved 2026-08-31 and valid 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12 under free-use/no-SLA terms, yields ten grouped stop areas. Its 27 national ferry shapes do not include Reuver-Kessel; the similarly named 'Reuver, Veer Kessel - Beesel' item is a bus stop, not ferry geometry or operating state.

NDW publishes CC0 DATEX II current images, speeds, incidents, planned works and temporary closures, with several national files changing within minutes at audit time. These can affect mobility/supply only while their observed or validity interval is current; absence or expiry is unknown, not proof of an open road.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Observed July 2021 high-water timeline, current ferry, climate context and Atlas Beesel 2050
evidenceSources.edition: observed incident July 2021; municipal pages and atlas accessed 2026-09-02
supports: The municipal incident log records evacuation return after dike inspection on 18 July 2021, three homes with substantial water nuisance, a high-water hole near the Schelkensbeek that closed Rijksweg, damage/closure on Kesselseweg and St. Jorisstraat, gas/electricity checks with Enexis, sandbags, unsafe seepage water and continuing dike inspection. This is observed historical evidence, not a current design-event calibration.

The current https://www.beesel.nl/inwoners/veerpont/ page says the Kessel-Reuver ferry operates daily for motor vehicles and light road traffic on published seasonal hours. The 2021 log records that the ferry and two roads reopened on 20 July, proving a flood-contingent local mobility state that the current graph omits.

Atlas Beesel 2050 at https://www.beesel.nl/data/downloadables/2/6/7/3/atlas-beesel-2050.pdf distinguishes the Maas valley floor, a low terrace, the middle terrace carrying Beesel, Offenbeek and Reuver, and the wooded high terrace/Brachter Wald toward Germany. It identifies the A73 as the main north-south road, weak east-west car links, Reuver station, the ferry and gaps in bus coverage.

The same official municipal material reports more than half a million annual overnight stays at De Lommerbergen, while the climate page at https://duurzaam.beesel.nl/inwoner/onze-ambassadeurs/aanpassen-aan-een-veranderend-klimaat identifies heat, drought and heavier-rain sewer overload. Registered residents therefore do not describe all people present or each hazard mechanism.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Beesel dike reinforcement, Limburg water-and-soil maps and public water assets
evidenceSources.edition: dike works completed 2022; HWH snapshot retrieved 2026-09-02
supports: The water board states that Beesel's former green-dike sections were too low and weak, that backflow behind the village and seepage required additional measures, and records completion of the reinforcement in October 2022. That defence change post-dates the 2021 incident and must be represented before replaying 2021 impact as present-day risk.

The current Water and Soil Underlay at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/over-ons/kaarten-en-data/onderlegger-water-bodem/ provides periodically updated, neighbourhood-scale official context/scenario maps for regional water nuisance, flood safety, drought, water availability, water quality and heat. It warns that source accuracy and climate/model assumptions differ; no reusable bulk API, fixed cadence or licence was found on that page, so it cannot drive the public simulation until those terms and layer metadata are pinned.

HWH/PDOK Kunstwerken IMWA is a national OGC API updated weekly under CC BY-SA 4.0; Waterketen DAMO is a public WFS/WMS/ATOM product under CC BY-SA 4.0 with incomplete contributor coverage. The current generated display-only snapshot contains 52 points inside Beesel: 48 weirs, two surface-water pumps and two sewer pumps, including emergency-pumping records at Huilbeek and Schelkensbeek/Rijksweg Zuid Reuver and sewer pumps at Reuver and Lommerbergen.

These points are official-context and affectsSimulation=false. A registered asset or status 'gerealiseerd' does not establish live operation, capacity, power dependency, backup, catchment, failure probability or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Provincial Risk Profile 2023–2027, Regional Crisis Plan 2024–2027 and first-72-hour guidance
supports: The current risk profile at https://www.vrln.nl/sites/vrln/files/2024-04/Veiligheidsregio_LN-ZL_Provinciaal_risicoprofiel.pdf covers river flood/dike breach, nature fire, heat, drought, cold, storm, earthquake, extreme rainfall, electricity/gas outage and large cyberattack. It is provincial, explicitly not municipality-specific, and calls for risks such as flood and nature fire to be represented more dynamically in space and time.

The crisis plan assigns population care to municipalities and the general public-safety chain, distinguishes functional chains, names WML for drinking water, Enexis/Gasunie for energy and Vodafone as regional telecom representative, and requires shared information and resource management rather than transferring operator control to the safety region.

The 2023–2026 high-water response plan, described at https://www.vrln.nl/nieuws/vernieuwde-rampbestrijdingsplan-hoogwater-vastgesteld, coordinates the safety regions with Rijkswaterstaat and Waterschap Limburg and links water levels to actions; its operational thresholds/resources are not encoded by the simulator.

Current VRLN guidance at https://www.vrln.nl/over-ons/wat-doet-de-veiligheidsregio/risicos-limburg-noord/noodpakket advises household supplies for 72 hours. It is normative preparedness guidance, not a measured Beesel readiness rate, operator restoration promise or evidence for the model's fixed 0.44 coefficient.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Near-real-time weather/seismic products and Maas water observations/forecasts
supports: KNMI station observations are issued every ten minutes, normally within minutes, may receive missing records for seven days and are CC BY 4.0. KNMI also publishes radar/nowcast and FDSN/ShakeMap products. Each is integration-ready only with product version, station/grid/event, validation status, time, resolution and licence retained.

Rijkswaterstaat explains at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/waterdata/waterstanden-en-afvoeren-rivieren that its network continuously measures water level and discharge and adds model forecasts. For the regulated Maas, discharge is emphasized over level; the four-day forecast is expert-validated and the 15-day plume is not. Historical water-height series can have ten-minute intervals.

Weather, water-level and seismic observations can initialize/replay an event but do not by themselves provide a Beesel neighbourhood flood footprint, service failure, smoke plume or 72-hour restoration forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public provider territories and bounded operator data for Beesel
evidenceSources.edition: live WMS/WFS query at municipal reference point; provider records lastUpdated 2025-09-07
supports: A reproducible GetFeatureInfo query at [6.0653243763, 51.2690845993] returns Enexis for electricity and gas, WML for drinking water, Ziggo for fixed media and no sewer provider record. The Public Domain, provider-supplied areas identify responsibility at one point, not complete municipal coverage, topology, redundancy or live state; empty sewer output is unknown, not no service.
VRLN independently identifies Enexis and WML for the region. Current map geometry is Liander-only and therefore offers no equivalent local Enexis cable, station or gas-pipe context in Beesel.

Enexis open data at https://www.enexis.nl/over-ons/waar-staan-wij-voor/open-data contains anonymized postcode consumption/generation and example congestion profiles, with dataset-specific currency and up to three years of history. It is useful baseline/context data, not feeder topology, outage state, available capacity or repair time.

WML's observed 2025 Maas contamination notice at https://www.wml.nl/over-wml/nieuws/verontreiniging-maas names parts of Beesel and documents temporary production switching from Maas water to deep groundwater with daily quality monitoring and no loss of availability. It evidences source substitution in that incident, not a reusable local topology or guarantee under all hazards.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Current machine-readable flood-risk and defence context
supports: The current ROR significant-flood-risk-area product is publicly available as WMS, WFS and ATOM/GML under CC0 and covers the Netherlands; its catalogue was updated 2026-08-05. It is official-context for screening and does not by itself supply a selected Beesel breach, local depth or arrival trajectory.

HWH Keringen IMWA provides machine-readable water-board defence geometry through WMS/WFS/ATOM under CC BY-SA 4.0; the catalogue warns that data is supplied by individual water boards. RWS water-defence products provide complementary normative context.

A simulation-driving river adapter still needs an expert-selected, versioned LIWO or Waterschap Limburg scenario with mechanism, defence state, depth/stress unit, probability, arrival, duration/recession, resolution, no-data semantics, licence and transformation hash.

identity.summary: GM0889 identity, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
notes: Feature id, generated regional bundle and manifest agree on Beesel, Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord.
The focused context resolved one expected municipality artifact and found no contradictory official identity.

geography.summary: The generalized 2025 municipality geometry and generated label point pass administrative checks, but are not hazard compartments.
notes: The generated center [6.0653243763, 51.2690845993] lies inside the generalized municipality boundary.

The municipal atlas distinguishes Maas valley floor, low, middle and wooded high terraces. The administrative boundary is not a hydraulic compartment, sewer catchment, forest fuel zone, utility feeder or response district.

demography.summary: Municipality totals and neighbourhood allocation reconcile within official publication rounding.
notes: Official 2025 population is 13,524, density is 485, 26.0% are aged 65 or older and there are 1,959 one-person households.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 13,515, nine below the municipality row (-0.067%); the local allocator reconciles exactly to 13,524.

Affected population is a resident-equivalent pressure count. It excludes tourists, commuters, visitors, pupils, patients, workers and people across the border or river; De Lommerbergen alone is reported at more than half a million annual overnight stays.

regionalDetail.summary: Neighbourhood coverage is complete for core demographics but several fields and activity/vulnerability dimensions remain unavailable.
notes: The bundle contains eight neighbourhoods in two districts with 36 statistic fields. Population, age, households, businesses, land and basic accessibility are complete.
Cars per household is missing in three neighbourhoods; district-heating share and public charging points are null in all eight and correctly remain unknown rather than zero.

No neighbourhood has an official zero resident count. Aggregate age and distance indicators do not identify individual vulnerability, daytime/overnight occupancy, facility dependence or restoration priority.

settlements.summary: BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlement concepts are retained distinctly.
notes: BAG woonplaatsen Beesel and Reuver have no generated center outside the generalized boundary.
BRT contains woonkernen Beesel and Reuver plus deelkern Bussereind. These features are descriptive settlement context, not resident totals, hazard zones, provider areas or response boundaries.

transport.summary: A73, station and scheduled-stop context are present, but the locally important cross-Maas motor ferry is absent from both the map ferry layer and the mobility/supply graph.
notes: The generated logical network has only two A73 links, north to Venlo and south to Roermond. Both nominal capacities are scenario units, not observed traffic or guaranteed emergency access.
Reuver station and ten grouped stops are official/scheduled context only. The stop called 'Reuver, Veer Kessel - Beesel' is not a ferry route or state.

Beesel says the Kessel-Reuver ferry runs daily for motor vehicles and light traffic; the 2021 log proves it can close under high water. Its omission removes the municipality's direct westbound link to GM1894 Peel en Maas and hides a first-72-hour mobility/supply decision.
NDW can add source-dated road incidents and closures, but an official/operator ferry-status adapter or a clearly dated manual incident input is still required.

emergencyContext.summary: Current regional roles and 72-hour guidance exist, but Beesel resources, transients and incident actions are not represented.
notes: The crisis plan separates municipal population care, water-manager responsibilities, functional utility chains and regional coordination; it does not give the simulator authority to operate utilities or promise restoration.
The 2021 Beesel log demonstrates time-stamped evacuation, dike inspection, sandbags, road/ferry closures, utility checks, cleanup and return. None are explicit model actions or resource states.

The model contains no warning/incident feed, role activation, evacuation zone, ferry/road passability, crews, emergency drinking-water points, shelter, medicines, backup fuel, stock, welfare checks, mutual aid or cross-border liaison state.
The fixed 0.44 household-preparedness coefficient is synthetic. VRLN's 72-hour checklist is advice, not measured readiness, and resident-only demand omits substantial visitor occupancy.

scenarioMatrix.summary: The complete deterministic 10 × 6 × 8 numerical contract passes for GM0889.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0889 pnpm audit:model passed all canonical presets at T+0, +6, +12, +24, +48 and +72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Selected T+24 synthetic outputs are: storm severity 0.1286 and 2,171 affected; pluvial 0.2278 and 1,431; river 0.1220 and 437; coastal direct severity zero and zero affected despite indirect wind/service deprivation; heat 0.0745 and 889; winter 0.5452 and 3,415; cyber 0.4038 and 4,781; earthquake current motion zero and zero affected; wildfire 0.1199 and 450; compound 0.8638 and 8,995.

At T+72 river remains strained with normalized inundation stress 0.3883, 711 affected and 144,747.57 cumulative event-attributable deprived person-hours. Compound remains critical with system pressure 0.6242, 9,225 affected and 504,758.87 person-hours. These are deterministic model outputs, not observations, forecasts or official decisions.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, exact no-event semantics, causal ledgers and local reconciliation pass.
notes: All tested values are finite and bounded, delivery does not exceed demand, repeated frames are deterministic, and hazard/service/system causal and counterfactual ledgers reconcile.
Intensity zero yields exact zero event hazard, zero affected population and zero event-attributable deprived person-hours for every preset and checkpoint.
Every local view contains eight neighbourhoods and reconciles exactly to 13,524 residents. Across services/presets the maximum demand, delivery or reconciliation error is 7.105427357601002e-15.

Local hazard is identical across the eight selected service maps, official null/zero semantics are preserved, and deprived person-hours are quarter-hour event-attributable shortfall relative to a matched no-event baseline.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The neighbourhood fields do not follow Beesel's distinct Maas, sewer, terrace, forest/smoke or cyber mechanisms.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound have exactly the same eight-neighbourhood rank: Beesel, Overige verspreide huizen, Bussereind, Offenbeek, Rijkel, Verspreide huizen ten oosten en zuiden van de spoorlijn, Verspreide huizen, Reuver.

Official context distinguishes a Maas valley/terrace system, urban sewer overload, named Schelkensbeek/Huilbeek controls and a wooded high terrace by Brachter Wald. One shared seeded order cannot represent all of those pathways.

River stress is derived from municipality-centroid distance to three hard-coded straight corridors, not the local Maas, defence, floodplain, breach, elevation, depth, arrival or recession. The post-2021 dike reinforcement is absent.

The wildfire source [5.75, 52.18] is 103.591 km from the municipal center. Beesel receives synthetic smoke but no event-specific wind plume; the preset cannot represent a local Brachter-Wald ignition. Coastal and earthquake direct local fields are zero at T+24.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight-service cascades are inspectable but not calibrated to Beesel operators, assets, ferry state, operating state or topology.
notes: All eight services receive the same two A73-derived municipal route records. Supplied/NWB connectivity is correctly disclosed as a logical transfer proxy, never physical electricity, drinking-water, drainage, gas/heating, telecom, facility or supply topology.

The display bundle now has 52 local HWH water/wastewater points, and provider areas identify Enexis, WML and Ziggo at the reference point. They correctly have affectsSimulation=false and do not establish connectivity, live condition, switching, flow, pressure, capacity, power dependency, backup or restoration.
Liander-only public electricity/gas geometry does not cover the responsible Beesel DSO. Enexis's public postcode aggregates are not a topology substitute.

The model has no typed ferry/passability state, Maas/sewer catchments, Enexis zones, WML supply zones, telecom service/control zones, verified critical-facility dependencies or emergency logistics stocks. No safe complete public source exists for all such operating relationships.

causalTrace.summary: Causal arithmetic and proxy wording are auditable, but local forcing and service coefficients remain largely synthetic.
notes: Hazard, availability, system-pressure and intervention ledgers reconcile and explanations disclose logical connectivity rather than utility topology.

For coastal flood at T+24, direct local inundation severity and normalized water stress are zero while 19.49 m/s wind causes indirect service deprivation; direct, indirect and cumulative effects must remain separate in maps and exports.

The public value called normalized inundation stress is not metres and does not select a hydraulic authority scenario. A historic closure or asset register point likewise does not prove a present failure.

Cyber disruption, household readiness, backup, network capacity, repair rates and service recovery have no Beesel operator calibration; regional role descriptions are governance evidence, not numeric coefficients.

recovery72h.summary: The first-72-hour window is numerically complete, but status transitions and restoration are not calibrated to the continuing hazard, local lifelines or responsible organizations.
notes: River forcing correctly persists through 72 hours under the 168-hour preset, but its unsupported amplitude yields 711 affected and 144,747.57 person-hours without a selected defence/breach scenario or ferry/road state.

Heat/drought forcing remains active through T+72 under the 336-hour preset while status is operational and affected residents are zero; winter and wildfire are also operational/zero affected. Cyber is recovering with zero affected. These threshold transitions are possible model states but not local health or operator evidence.

Cumulative T+72 deprived person-hours are storm 157,112.30; pluvial 106,475.25; coastal 56,683.07; heat 61,487.52; winter 180,408.59; cyber 191,858.18; earthquake 1,585.93; wildfire 55,278.34. Exact recovery rates are assumptions, not promises.

The observed 2021 timeline shows that dike checks, return, individual road repair, ferry reopening, utility checks and seepage safety each had distinct clocks. Current regional 72-hour guidance concerns household preparedness, not universal service restoration.

findings.summary: The locally important Maas preset reports exact persistent Beesel impact without a selected hydraulic or defence scenario.
findings.evidence: At T+24/T+72 the derived screen reports normalized inundation stress 0.3883, with 437 then 711 affected residents and 144,747.57 cumulative person-hours at T+72. E03 records real 2021 evacuations, closures and seepage effects, but E04 records material dike/backflow/seepage reinforcement completed afterward in 2022. The model uses centroid distance to three hard-coded straight corridors and has no local Maas geometry, selected breach/defence state, elevation, depth, arrival or recession input.
findings.action: Mark the present direct amplitude and affected/service totals unsupported—not safe—and do not present them as calibrated until an expert-selected LIWO or Waterschap Limburg scenario is sampled. Integrate current HWH/RWS defence geometry and store mechanism, breach/scenario ID, defence edition, depth/stress unit, probability, arrival, duration/recession, resolution, no-data, licence, hash and reviewer. Preserve indirect regional effects separately; never calibrate current impact directly from the pre-reinforcement 2021 incident.

findings.summary: Eight physically different nonzero hazards reuse one Beesel neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: The T+24 probe finds exactly the same order for storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound: Beesel first and Reuver last, with the same six neighbourhoods between them. E03-E04 distinguish the Maas/terraces, sewer overload, Schelkensbeek/Huilbeek controls and wooded high terrace; cyber has no reason to share any physical-hazard footprint.
findings.action: Replace shared seeded modulation with hazard-specific spatial adapters and regression tests. Sample versioned hydraulic/pluvial rasters, AHN/BGT surfaces, heat/land-cover and fuel/weather/plume inputs; select cyber/service zones explicitly. Retain evidence class, native resolution, no-data, time, licence, transform hash and uncertainty, and prove different mechanisms do not rank all neighbourhoods identically solely because they share a seed.

findings.summary: The daily Reuver-Kessel motor ferry is missing from both the ferry map and mobility/supply graph.
findings.evidence: The current graph has only A73 links from GM0889 to Venlo and Roermond; OVapi's ferry layer has no Reuver-Kessel shape, and its similarly named Reuver stop is a bus stop. E03 says the ferry connects Reuver to Kessel/GM1894 daily for motor vehicles and light traffic, while the 2021 incident log records high-water unavailability and reopening on 20 July. The omission removes a real cross-Maas lifeline and its hazard-contingent state.
findings.action: Add an audited GM0889-GM1894 ferry lifeline for mobility and supply only, using official municipal/operator service identity and BGT/NWB/authority-confirmed landing geometry. Keep capacity as declared scenario units until observed vehicle/trip data exists. Add open/closed/unknown and valid-time state from a licensed operator feed when available, otherwise a clearly source-dated manual incident input; river high water must be able to close it without affecting utility graphs.

findings.summary: Public local water-control context and observed Schelkensbeek road failure do not influence pluvial/drainage exposure.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports one municipal stress 0.3154 and 1,431 affected, then allocates the common seed order. E03 records the 2021 Rijksweg hole at Schelkensbeek and municipal sewer-overload concerns. E04 shows 52 display-only local HWH points, including emergency pumps at Schelkensbeek/Rijksweg Zuid Reuver and Huilbeek and sewer pumps at Reuver/Lommerbergen, but none affects the model and most lack public capacity/state.
findings.action: Ingest a versioned Waterschap Limburg/municipal pluvial stress raster and water-system/catchment geometry; intersect it with neighbourhoods, the A73/local roads, ferry access and typed facilities. Keep registered points as context until operating state, power/backup and capacity are sourced. Treat the 2021 failure as validation/replay evidence, not deterministic proof of present failure after subsequent works.

findings.summary: Two A73 records are reused as logical transfer proxies for all eight services, not Beesel utility topology.
findings.evidence: Every service view receives the same two road records. E05/E07 identify Enexis, WML, Gasunie and telecom functional-chain participants, while the point provider lookup returns Enexis/WML/Ziggo and no sewer record. Liander-only geometry does not cover the Beesel DSO; Enexis aggregates, provider polygons and HWH points reveal neither connected topology nor live switching, flow, pressure, backup or restoration.
findings.action: Separate mobility/supply routing from non-mobility service graphs. Use provider areas, HWH points and operator aggregates only as official context. Where no safe public topology exists, use the smallest editable synthetic zonal graph with ranges and sensitivity analysis, visibly label it synthetic, and never infer feeders, pipes, telecom links or restoration from NWB proximity.

findings.summary: Resident-only pressure and coarse facility context omit material visitor and continuity demand.
findings.evidence: E01 reports 13,524 registered residents and 26.0% aged 65 or older. E03 reports more than half a million annual overnight stays at De Lommerbergen and a stop name at that site. The model contains no separately sourced visitor/patient/worker occupancy or typed, operational care, shelter, school, emergency-service and supply nodes; a stop or KVK address cannot establish facility role, capacity, backup, staffing or open state.
findings.action: Create a typed, dated facility/transient-exposure registry from RIVM acute-care fixtures, CIBG/LRZa after access review, DUO, BAG/KVK and authority-confirmed sites. Keep registered residents, visitors, workers and patients as separate denominators. Require source, valid time, function and confidence; keep occupancy, backup, staffing, medicines, shelter and operational state unknown unless explicitly sourced.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour response is a generic coefficient rather than a time-stamped role, decision and resource model.
findings.evidence: E05 defines municipal population care, regional information/resource management and functional utility chains, while VRLN's 72-hour material is household guidance. E03's observed log has distinct evacuation, dike inspection, road/ferry closure, sandbag, utility-check, cleanup and return actions. The simulator has none of those states and no Beesel evidence for householdPreparedness=0.44.
findings.action: Add a provenance-bearing incident timeline with official observed, official scenario, synthetic or unknown class for warning/source time, role/team activation, incident/evacuation areas, closures, ferry state, dike inspection, verified crews, emergency water, shelter, medicines, fuel, stocks, welfare checks, mutual aid and cross-border liaison. Retain 0.44 only as an editable synthetic assumption, never measured readiness or a restoration guarantee.

findings.summary: Fixed Groningen-earthquake and distant-wildfire presets do not cover locally selectable Limburg event mechanisms.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the Groningen-earthquake preset has zero current ground motion in Beesel and peak severity 0.0046. The wildfire source is 103.591 km away and yields zero direct flame but smoke 0.2349 without an event-specific wind plume. E03 places wooded high terrace/Brachter Wald context at Beesel; E05 lists earthquake/nature fire and VRLN explains that Limburg has Peelrand/Feldbiss tectonic mechanisms. E06 exposes KNMI event/ShakeMap and weather products.
findings.action: Keep the current presets explicitly source-specific. Add editable event selection: KNMI FDSN/ShakeMap for a Limburg earthquake and a locally selected ignition/perimeter with authoritative land cover/fuel, KNMI wind/humidity and uncertainty for fire/smoke. Do not imply that a distant preset is a complete municipal risk assessment or turn regional nature-fire phase into a local burn footprint.

findings.summary: Direct, indirect, historic and defence-conditioned flood evidence need explicit separation.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 has zero direct local inundation but 19.49 m/s wind and cumulative service deprivation. River stress 0.3883 is normalized and non-hydraulic. The 2021 municipal timeline is observed before the completed 2022 dike reinforcement, while HWH/ROR products are register/risk context and the Water and Soil Underlay is modelled scenario context. Without evidence class and mechanism in every view, these can be mistaken for live depth or current expected damage.
findings.action: Show direct inundation, wind, seepage/backwater, road/ferry and downstream network contributions separately in legend, inspector, brief and export. Always show event/scenario, evidence class, source/valid time, defence assumption and confidence. Never label normalized inundation stress as metres, an old incident as a present forecast, or no-data/zero direct coast impact as proof of no indirect disruption.

findings.summary: First-72-hour status and restoration trajectories are not calibrated to Beesel hazards, operators or lifelines.
findings.evidence: At T+72 river remains strained and compound critical; heat, winter and wildfire are operational/zero affected despite continuing or recently ended forcing, while cyber is recovering/zero affected. The model accumulates exact service person-hours but has no ferry/road repair state, operator switching/restoration, emergency water, care continuity or resource timeline. E03 shows these clocks differed in the actual 2021 response, and E05 assigns them to different responsible chains.
findings.action: Calibrate hazard/status thresholds, backup endurance and recovery separately by service and incident class with responsible authorities/operators. Treat observed outage/closure/resource feeds as valid only for their timestamps. Report ranges and uncertainty, separate service restoration from household preparedness and hazard duration, and expose unresolved/unknown states instead of an exact unqualified trajectory.

findings.summary: The current deterministic accounting and proxy semantics pass the Beesel harness.
findings.evidence: The focused matrix passes finite bounds, determinism, exact zero-event behavior, causal/counterfactual reconciliation, event-attributable person-hours, preserved official null/zero semantics, service-invariant local hazard and exact municipality/local population-demand-delivery totals. Public wording identifies NWB connectivity as a logical transfer proxy and normalized inundation stress as non-hydraulic; public water/utility assets are context-only and affectsSimulation=false.
findings.action: Retain these invariants in the national gate and add GM0889 regressions for selected hydraulic evidence, hazard-specific neighbourhood fields, the Reuver-Kessel ferry state, operator/context boundaries and direct-versus-indirect flood semantics before accepting the open corrections.

corrections.summary: Replace Beesel's exact Maas proximity output with an evidence-bearing, defence-conditioned hydraulic scenario.
corrections.validation: GM0889 river output is visibly unsupported/unknown until a versioned selected scenario is loaded; it never claims current metres or expected affected residents from centroid distance. A loaded scenario records local Maas mechanism, defence/breach state including post-2022 geometry, depth/stress unit, probability, arrival, persistence/recession, native resolution, no-data, licence, hash and reviewer, and samples neighbourhood/road/facility footprints deterministically.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared Beesel neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific spatial adapters.
corrections.validation: Storm, pluvial, river, heat/drought, winter, cyber, wildfire/smoke and compound no longer reproduce one identical neighbourhood order solely from a shared seed. Tests retain service-layer invariance for a chosen hazard while validating source-specific geometry, time, no-data, provenance and uncertainty.

corrections.summary: Add the audited Reuver-Kessel ferry as a hazard-contingent mobility/supply lifeline.
corrections.validation: A source-backed ferry route connects GM0889 and GM1894 only for mobility/supply, uses authoritative landing geometry and declared scenario-unit capacity, appears on the ferry map and logical graph, and supports open/closed/unknown with valid time. A high-water closure removes ferry transfer without deleting the A73 or changing power/water/gas/telecom graphs.

corrections.summary: Integrate Limburg pluvial/water-system data without promoting register assets to live causal nodes.
corrections.validation: A version-pinned pluvial raster and catchment/terrain inputs drive neighbourhood and road/facility exposure with explicit no-data. All 52 current HWH points retain publisher, manager, source timestamp, licence, coverage and context-only/causal status; missing capacity, power, backup and operating state remain unknown and no point causes a failure merely by existing.

corrections.summary: Separate mobility/supply from utility graphs and add typed facilities, transients and first-72-hour response state.
corrections.validation: Provider areas/HWH/operator aggregates remain official context and roads/ferry do not silently become utility topology. Registered residents, visitors/workers/patients and facility occupancy are separate. Warnings, roles, incident/evacuation area, closures, inspections, crews, emergency water, shelter, medicine, fuel, stocks, welfare checks and mutual aid show observed/official-scenario/synthetic/unknown provenance and as-of time.

corrections.summary: Connect event forcing and recovery to versioned authoritative inputs while preserving direct/indirect semantics.
corrections.validation: Weather, water and seismic values declare observation, forecast, warning, official scenario or synthetic mode with product/version, time, resolution, validation and licence. Limburg quake/local ignition selection is possible. Direct inundation, indirect wind/seepage/network and cumulative deprivation remain separate, and service recovery uses calibrated ranges independent of household readiness and forcing duration.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides safe, complete and current Enexis electricity/gas feeder and switching topology, WML pressure/supply topology, sewer control, telecom control, critical-facility backup, crews, fuel, stock or restoration order for Beesel. These must not be inferred from roads, provider areas or public points.

Mijn Aansluiting provider records at the municipal reference point identify Enexis, WML and Ziggo but not full-boundary coverage, connectivity, redundancy, quality or live state; the empty sewer response is unknown.

HWH water/wastewater registries have contributor-dependent completeness. 'Gerealiseerd' and feature timestamps do not prove live operation, condition, available capacity, power supply, backup or failure.

The Limburg Water and Soil Underlay is periodically updated official model/context material, but its public page does not state a reusable bulk API, fixed cadence or licence for every layer. Terms and per-layer metadata must be secured before ingestion.
ROR risk areas and defence registers are not a selected depth/arrival scenario. LIWO or water-board scenario choice and expert review are still required for simulation-driving flood output.
The municipal 2021 high-water log is invaluable observed validation evidence but predates the completed 2022 dike reinforcement and cannot be used as an unchanged present-day damage curve.

OVapi GTFS is planned service without an SLA and omits the local motor ferry; NDW does not guarantee ferry state. Neither a transit stop nor absence of a current record proves operation or passability.
CBS statistics describe registered residents and rounded annual aggregates, not people present, individual vulnerability, tourists, commuters, patients, facility occupancy or response priority.

KNMI station/radar and RWS Waterinfo products are observed/forecast environmental inputs, not neighbourhood flood, smoke, service-failure or restoration products; spatial transformation and uncertainty require validation.

Exact hazard intensities, service availabilities, affected totals, backup hours, flows, interventions and deprived person-hours remain synthetic or derived-screening outputs, not operator commitments, observations, forecasts or official emergency decisions.
The audit covers display hours 0–72. High water, heat/drought, contamination, displacement, infrastructure repair, ecological/agricultural effects and recovery can continue beyond that horizon.
provinceReviewFlags: Audit all Limburg Maas municipalities with current dike/defence editions and expert-selected LIWO/Waterschap Limburg mechanisms; do not substitute three straight river corridors or pre-reinforcement 2021 effects for hydraulic connectivity.

Require distinct pluvial, river, heat/drought, winter/storm, nature-fire/smoke and cyber neighbourhood fields across Limburg. The common canonical seed/order is a national model defect, not Beesel-specific noise.

Create an audited Limburg ferry/lifeline catalogue covering Reuver-Kessel and other non-GTFS motor ferries, with authoritative landing geometry, supported services, scenario-unit capacity, operator/state source and flood/ice/wind closure semantics.

Use Waterschap Limburg Underlay/scenario layers, HWH water assets, RWS/PDOK flood-risk/defence layers, Waterinfo and KNMI products with explicit official-context, official-scenario, observed or forecast provenance; retain no-data and licence per layer.

Separate NWB/NDW mobility from electricity, drinking water, drainage, gas/heating, telecom, facilities and emergency-supply topology across Limburg. Provider areas and Enexis/WML aggregates are context, while missing/security-sensitive operating topology remains unknown or transparently synthetic.

Add Limburg-selectable earthquake and nature-fire/smoke events, cross-border German context where relevant, transient recreation/tourism demand, typed critical facilities and a source-dated first-72-hour role/resource contract.
